subtopic: Triton GEMM / FP16 inputs, FP32 accumulation
learningObjective: Reason about the FP16-in / FP32-out matmul pattern common in Triton GEMM kernels and why FP32 accumulation is used.
stem: Consider the Triton GEMM inner loop below. Which statements about the `tl.dot` call and accumulator precision are correct? (Select all that apply.)
codeSnippet:
# A, B, C: FP16 row-major; K-loop accumulator = FP32
acc = tl.zeros((BM, BN), dtype=tl.float32)
for k in range(0, K, BK):
    a = tl.load(A_block_ptr)          # FP16, [BM, BK]
    b = tl.load(B_block_ptr)          # FP16, [BK, BN]
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, out_dtype=tl.float32)   # accumulate in FP32
    A_block_ptr = tl.advance(A_block_ptr, (0, BK))
    B_block_ptr = tl.advance(B_block_ptr, (BK, 0))
c = acc.to(tl.float16)                # cast back to FP16 for storage
tl.store(C_block_ptr, c)

options.text: FP32 accumulation is only necessary in Triton; CUDA's native `wmma`/`mma.sync` APIs are limited to FP16 accumulation and cannot mix input/accumulator precisions on Ampere or Hopper.

FP32 accumulation is used to avoid catastrophic loss of precision when summing many FP16 partials: FP16's ~3-decimal-digit precision cannot faithfully represent large partial sums that arise from long K-dimension reductions.

On Ampere+, `tl.dot(a, b, out_dtype=tl.float32)` with FP16 inputs lowers to Tensor Core MMA instructions (mma.sync) that accept FP16 operands and produce FP32 accumulator lanes natively, matching the hardware's design.

Casting `acc.to(tl.float16)` at the end is guaranteed to produce a bit-identical result to running the entire kernel in FP16 including accumulation, because FP32→FP16 rounding is a no-op when values are within FP16 range.

explanation: A: FP16 has only ~11 bits of mantissa; long reductions accumulate rounding error. FP32 accumulation preserves precision. B: On sm_80+, Tensor Core `mma.sync` instructions natively accept FP16 operands with FP32 accumulator (`mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.f16.f16.f32` and similar). Triton's `tl.dot(..., out_dtype=tl.float32)` compiles to these. C is wrong: FP32-accumulate then downcast produces a different (usually much more accurate) result than FP16-accumulate. D is wrong: CUDA `wmma`/`mma.sync` explicitly support mixed-precision (FP16-in, FP32-accum) on Volta, Turing, Ampere, Hopper — that is one of Tensor Cores' key features.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: mixed-precision Tensor Core support is a core feature of CUDA's mma APIs.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: FP32 accumulation is standard for numerical robustness.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: mma.sync FP16-in, FP32-accum is the hardware path on Ampere+.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: FP32-accum-then-downcast ≠ full-FP16 pipeline; the intermediate precision matters.

assumptions: Tensor Core support on the target GPU (sm_70+).
Triton compiler lowers `tl.dot` with mixed dtypes to mma.sync when supported.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP32 accumulation eliminates all rounding error; it dramatically reduces it but is not exact.
Does not imply FP16 accumulation is always wrong; short reductions may be acceptable.

distractorRationales.A: Fabricates a limitation of CUDA mma APIs.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses same-precision cast with true mixed-precision equivalence.
